correctness.rationale: Finite exhaustive proof across the complete four-named-colour domain of \(4^{14}\) states using two separate graph models and enumeration implementations. Explicit checked 14-vertex isomorphism; sound partial pruning in Fano DFS and independent full predicate at proper leaves in LCF traversal. Both reproduce exactly 54,264 states, six support-profile totals, 185,808 one-vertex transitions, 6,048 isolated states, eight 882-components, six 6,860-components, 897,456 exact-two-vertex transitions and one connected exact-two-change graph. The independent Fano property-B counting argument proves three colours impossible; finite enumeration gives four-colour existence. No claim extends to untested graph orders.

originality.rationale: The exact novel claim concerns the four-named-colour Heawood locally-identifying configuration and Hamming-one/two exchange graph. Esperet et al. provide the definition, bipartite four-colour bound and three-colour hypergraph criterion, which already imply the minimum four and are explicitly credited. They do not give the full four-colour census or its exchange components. Foucaud et al.'s recolouring lemma needs more than twelve colours on a cubic graph and does not imply four-colour connectivity. The 2023 product work treats different graph families and minima, not this graph's exchange state space. Nearby mathematical records involve ordinary three-colour Heawood recolouring, different dominated-colouring constraints or a joined-clique lid polynomial. No matching statement or stronger result implying it was found in checked materials. This remains a provisional historical originality assessment, not universal novelty certification.
residual_risks: The accessible indexed search is incomplete; an unindexed published census or prior computational table may coincide exactly.
Some published record summaries were available without their entire original result folders; implication was checked only at the reported statement level.
The scientific result has not received independent scholarly validation; two code implementations are not a substitute for outside checking.

value.rationale: The new object is the full optimal solution reconfiguration space of the canonical Fano incidence graph for a natural local colour-identification requirement. Its exact classification exposes 6,048 frozen optimal assignments, fourteen nontrivial palette-support sectors and a sharp single-to-double simultaneous-change connectivity threshold, quantitatively resolving a question not implied by the already-known chromatic minimum. The frozen states and shore/core sectors are mathematically motivated by non-two-colourability of the underlying projective plane, and make the precise finite fact reusable in constrained recolouring and configuration-space comparisons.
